title: Does Print Size Matter for Reading?
locator: Print Size Metrics; x-height; fluent range; low-vision discussion
claim: Reading depends on visual angle and glyph metrics, not CSS font size alone.
limitations: Review plus historical surveys; not a web font-size prescription.

title: Towards Individuated Reading Experiences
claim: Font preference and effectiveness diverge; no font was consistently fastest across all readers.
limitations: 352 retained US readers; Times/Noto Sans/preferred/two random fonts per person; remote timing/visual size; reading disabilities excluded.

title: Quantifying Visual Preferences Around the World
locator: Method pp.3–4; model pp.4–5; limitations p.9
claim: Visual appeal preferences vary across sampled people and groups.
limitations: English instructions; self-selection; group correlations are not causes, individual predictions, or usability outcomes.

title: Role of visual complexity and prototypicality in first impressions
locator: Author/publisher abstract; full Google PDF inaccessible
claim: Brief screenshot exposure produced complexity/prototypicality effects on aesthetic ratings.
limitations: Abstract inspected; full methods unavailable in this pass; no claim of observed task usability.

title: Keep it Simple: How Visual Complexity and Preferences Impact Search Efficiency
claim: Low-complexity screenshots supported faster target search in the sampled task.
limitations: Different real websites confound features; forced fast search; recall excludes do-not-know answers (121 participants); preference filtering.

title: Rethinking perceptual organization: uniform connectedness
claim: Connected regions can compete with proximity/similarity in perceptual grouping.
context: Controlled visual demonstrations and proposed theory
limitations: Not a trial of cards, CSS spacing scales, or real product task performance.

title: The proper placement of uniform connectedness
claim: Challenges the serial-processing interpretation of Palmer/Rock.
limitations: Does not refute every practical grouping effect; cannot supply UI pixel values.

title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2
locator: Abstract; conformance; criteria addressed in VIS-09–14
claim: Conformance criteria and levels must be identified accurately.
limitations: Conformance does not address every disability-related need or establish overall usability.

title: Understanding Text Spacing
claim: Content must tolerate specified user spacing overrides without lost content/function.
limitations: Values are override-tolerance tests, not mandatory authored defaults; script exceptions apply.

title: Understanding Reflow
claim: Reflow tests vertical content at 320 CSS px width, horizontal content at 256 CSS px height; essential two-dimensional exceptions apply.
limitations: Table cells and surrounding controls still need consideration; not every table must become cards.

title: Understanding Contrast Minimum
claim: Text contrast has size-dependent thresholds and exceptions.
limitations: Thin rendering can remain weak despite nominal ratios; logo and inactive-element exceptions are scoped.

title: Understanding Non-text Contrast
claim: Required identification/state graphics need contrast against adjacent colors.
limitations: Not every decorative border needs 3:1; inactive/user-agent/essential-graphic exceptions differ.

title: Understanding Focus Appearance
claim: AAA focus indicator area/contrast differs from merely having visible focus.
limitations: Two-pixel perimeter equivalent is area criterion, not an unconditional outline implementation mandate.

title: Understanding Animation from Interactions
claim: Nonessential interaction-triggered motion can be disabled.
limitations: Automatic motion has separate criteria; essential animation exception; more than aesthetic preference.

title: Requirements for Hangul Text Layout and Typography
locator: Status; §4.1 fonts; §7.1 line breaking and restrictions
claim: Hangul text can break by character or word; punctuation constraints and mixed-script metrics matter.
limitations: Group Note Draft, explicitly not an endorsed Recommendation; contains unfinished sections.

title: Structural markup and right-to-left text in HTML
locator: Quick answer; base direction; language tags; tables
claim: Set base direction semantically and use logical layout properties.
limitations: Language and direction are separate; inline bidi cases need additional handling.

title: GOV.UK type scale
claim: Typography combines size and line-height roles and responsive behavior.
limitations: System-specific values; not universal legal or perceptual minimums.

title: Using the updated type scale
claim: A foundational typography update requires retesting custom layout and positioning.
limitations: Migration instructions apply to corresponding Frontend versions.

title: Making GOV.UK typography more accessible
locator: Why changing; specific changes; testing plans
claim: Explains reasons for removing very small sizes and preserving small-text size on mobile.
limitations: Community feedback and design rationale, not controlled effect-size evidence; published plan later evolved.

title: Carbon data table guidelines
claim: Density variants and layout treatments depend on table content and task.
limitations: Documented conventions, not measured superiority; not a spreadsheet replacement. Live sizing table visually inspected.

title: Atlassian typography
locator: Brand/app fonts; text styles/tokens; heading table
claim: Uses distinct brand/product fonts and bold heading tokens.
limitations: House system cannot determine all products’ fonts or semantic hierarchy policies.

title: Designing accessible color systems
locator: Background; Visualizing color; Results; badge example
claim: Perceptual palette tooling helped coordinate contrast, hue and visual weight.
limitations: Firsthand process report; claimed pair-spacing guarantees apply to that palette. Contrast figure visually inspected in browser.

title: Responsive Design for Motion
claim: Alternate motion treatments can preserve intent while avoiding specific triggers.
limitations: 2017 cases are historical, not current browser-support tests; no medical prevalence claim adopted.

title: Editorial New case study
claim: Expressive interaction is tied to demonstrating a variable typeface.
limitations: Agency account; awards do not prove task usability or accessibility; no live flow tested.

title: Building a Visual Language at Airbnb
locator: Getting to work; Foundation; Components; Lessons Learned
claim: Audited real screens and iterated foundations and purposeful components.
limitations: Historical practitioner account; claimed speed/quality not independently measured here.

title: Reimagining Design Systems at Spotify
locator: GLUE history; Encore layers and local systems
claim: System structure addressed autonomy and many platforms.
limitations: Author-preserved original; 2020 intent must be compared with later results.

title: Encore Three Years On
claim: Later experience prompted more reusable components and semantic token layers.
limitations: Self-report; adoption metrics do not establish customer experience; no independent audit.

title: System of systems: What we didn’t see coming
locator: Hidden load; local success; promotion pipeline
claim: Reports maintenance/governance costs and a successful denser business subsystem.
limitations: Author now consults; reported 20% result lacks public raw experiment details; not causal proof of density benefit.

title: How Spotify’s design system goes beyond platforms
claim: Shared component language can preserve platform-specific focus, size and interaction behavior.
limitations: Spotify manager account hosted by Figma; not independent corroboration of outcomes.

title: ui.sh design skill and relevant local rules
claim: Mixes reusable implementation guidance with strong font, weight and spacing house rules.
limitations: Local provenance/license not established; no execution efficacy measured.

title: Taster skill and brand reference
claim: Connects taxonomy, tokens, detector levels and brand; acknowledges detector limits.

title: Anthropic frontend-design skill
claim: Connects distinctive choices to brief while allowing explicitly requested aesthetics.

title: Baseline UI skill

title: Vercel web-design-guidelines skill

title: Vercel Web Interface Guidelines command
claim: Code-review rubric spans semantics, layout robustness, motion and rendering concerns.
limitations: Inspecting rubric does not establish performance, aesthetic quality or universal applicability.

title: Measuring visual clutter
